name: Bow tie

card.summary: A bow tie is self-tied or clip-on neckwear that frames the lower face and jaw and gives a sharp, formal or distinctive look.

quick.overview:
A bow tie is a small knotted band of fabric worn at the collar. It sits right under the jaw, so it draws the eye up toward the face and neck and reads as a deliberate, polished style choice.

It traces to the cravat tradition of the 17th to 19th centuries and is the classic piece for black-tie and white-tie evening wear. It also has a reputation as a distinctive or quirky accent in everyday dress.
quick.how: Wearers choose between self-tie (the traditional strip tied by hand), pre-tied and clip-on versions, and shapes such as bat wing, butterfly and diamond point. Self-tied versions are the usual choice for formal evening wear.
quick.risks: No health risks. Fit of the collar and the size of the bow relative to the face and neck affect how it looks, and commentators note it can carry associations with conservatism or nerdiness depending on context.

lead: A bow tie is a neckwear piece made from a strip of fabric tied in a symmetrical bow at the collar. Types include pre-tied (a bow sewn onto a neck band), clip-on, and the traditional self-tie, also called freestyle.[1]

For appearance, it works as a style accessory that frames the jaw and lower face and signals formality. It is the classic neckwear of black-tie and white-tie evening dress, and is also worn by classical musicians, at weddings, and by some people as a signature look.[1]

Its history is tied to the cravat: scarves worn by Croatian mercenaries during the Thirty Years' War were adopted by the French upper classes, and historians are unsure whether the cravat evolved into the bow tie and the four-in-hand necktie or the bow tie came first.[1]

chain: Small bow sits just below the jaw
Draws the eye to the face and neck
angle.text: A bow tie places a compact accent right under the face, so people use it to look polished and to add a memorable focal point at the collar. Choice of shape and size changes how it frames the jaw.

paras: Pre-tied bow ties are sewn to a band that clips closed, clip-on versions attach directly to collar points, and the self-tie is the traditional strip tied by hand.[1] Common shapes are the bat wing with parallel sides, the thistle or butterfly, and the diamond point, which is pointed at both ends.[1] Fixed-length ties suit formal wing-collar shirts, while adjustable ties suit softer collars.[1]

Black-tie and white-tie evening wear is the classic setting, and bow ties are also common at weddings and among classical musicians. Ready-tied versions are generally considered a faux pas at black- or white-tie events but are common at occasions such as school proms.[1] Pediatricians often wear them because infants cannot grab them the way they can a necktie.[1] In the 1980s some professional women wore them with tailored suits.[1]

Commentators have noted both a possible comeback among men and a reputation for conservatism and nerdiness.[1] Public figures known for wearing them include the biochemist Fritz Lipmann, Belgian prime minister Elio Di Rupo, Bill Nye and Paul Reubens as Pee-wee Herman.[1]

timeline.event: Croatian mercenaries in the Thirty Years' War wear neck scarves later adopted in France as cravats.[1]
French upper classes adopt the cravat; related styles such as the lavalliere appear.[1]
